"""User entity - Core authentication and user management

Represents a user account with authentication, authorization, and relationship tracking.
Users own flows, folders, variables, and API keys. Supports profile customization,
activity tracking, and opt-in feature tracking.
"""

type User {
  "Unique identifier for the user"
  id: UUID!
  
  "Unique username for authentication"
  username: String!
  
  "Hashed password for authentication"
  password: String!
  
  "Optional profile image URL or path"
  profile_image: String
  
  "Indicates if the user account is active"
  is_active: Boolean!
  
  "Indicates if the user has superuser privileges"
  is_superuser: Boolean!
  
  "Timestamp when the user account was created"
  create_at: DateTime!
  
  "Timestamp when the user account was last updated"
  updated_at: DateTime!
  
  "Timestamp of the user's last login"
  last_login_at: DateTime
  
  "Store API key for marketplace integration"
  store_api_key: String
  
  "User opt-in preferences and actions"
  optins: UserOptin
  
  "API keys associated with this user"
  api_keys: [ApiKey!]!
  
  "Flows created by this user"
  flows: [Flow!]!
  
  "Global variables owned by this user"
  variables: [Variable!]!
  
  "Folders/projects owned by this user"
  folders: [Folder!]!
}

"""User opt-in tracking for various features and actions"""
type UserOptin {
  "User has starred the GitHub repository"
  github_starred: Boolean!
  
  "User has dismissed the dialog"
  dialog_dismissed: Boolean!
  
  "User has clicked the Discord link"
  discord_clicked: Boolean!
}

"""Input type for creating a new user"""
input UserCreateInput {
  "Username for the new user (must be unique)"
  username: String!
  
  "Password for the new user"
  password: String!
  
  "Optional opt-in preferences"
  optins: UserOptinInput
}

"""Input type for updating a user"""
input UserUpdateInput {
  "New username (must be unique if changed)"
  username: String
  
  "New profile image URL"
  profile_image: String
  
  "New password"
  password: String
  
  "Update active status"
  is_active: Boolean
  
  "Update superuser status"
  is_superuser: Boolean
  
  "Update last login timestamp"
  last_login_at: DateTime
  
  "Update opt-in preferences"
  optins: UserOptinInput
}

input UserOptinInput {
  github_starred: Boolean
  dialog_dismissed: Boolean
  discord_clicked: Boolean
}
nodes.impact_analysis: Add role_assignments relationship to UserRoleAssignment. Maintain is_superuser flag for backward compatibility (H2).

nodes.name: Flow
nodes.description: Represents a visual workflow/flow in LangBuilder. Flows contain nodes and edges defining the logic pipeline, can be components or full applications, and support webhooks, MCP integration, and various access types. Each flow belongs to a user and optionally to a folder.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""Flow entity - Visual workflow/pipeline representation

Represents a complete workflow with nodes and edges, supporting component reuse,
webhook endpoints, MCP server integration, and public/private access control.
Flows can be locked for editing and support rich metadata (icons, colors, tags).
"""

type Flow {
  "Unique identifier for the flow"
  id: UUID!
  
  "Name of the flow (must be unique per user)"
  name: String!
  
  "Optional description of the flow's purpose"
  description: String
  
  "Icon representation (emoji or lucide icon name)"
  icon: String
  
  "Background color for the icon (hex format #RRGGBB)"
  icon_bg_color: String
  
  "Gradient style for visual representation"
  gradient: String
  
  "Flow data structure containing nodes and edges"
  data: FlowData
  
  "Indicates if this flow is a reusable component"
  is_component: Boolean
  
  "Timestamp of last update"
  updated_at: DateTime
  
  "Indicates if flow can be accessed via webhook endpoint"
  webhook: Boolean
  
  "URL-safe endpoint name for API access (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores)"
  endpoint_name: String
  
  "Tags for categorization and search"
  tags: [String!]
  
  "Indicates if the flow is locked from editing"
  locked: Boolean
  
  "Indicates if flow is exposed in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server"
  mcp_enabled: Boolean
  
  "Name of the MCP action associated with this flow"
  action_name: String
  
  "Description of the MCP action"
  action_description: String
  
  "Access control type for the flow"
  access_type: AccessType!
  
  "ID of the user who owns this flow"
  user_id: UUID
  
  "User who owns this flow"
  user: User
  
  "ID of the folder containing this flow"
  folder_id: UUID
  
  "Folder containing this flow"
  folder: Folder
  
  "Filesystem path for file-based flows"
  fs_path: String
}

"""Flow data structure containing the visual graph"""
type FlowData {
  "List of nodes in the flow"
  nodes: [FlowNode!]!
  
  "List of edges connecting nodes"
  edges: [FlowEdge!]!
}

"""Node in a flow graph"""
type FlowNode {
  "Unique node identifier within the flow"
  id: String!
  
  "Node type/class"
  type: String!
  
  "Node configuration and data"
  data: JSON!
  
  "Visual position of the node"
  position: Position
}

"""Edge connecting two nodes in a flow"""
type FlowEdge {
  "Unique edge identifier"
  id: String!
  
  "Source node ID"
  source: String!
  
  "Target node ID"
  target: String!
  
  "Source handle ID"
  sourceHandle: String
  
  "Target handle ID"
  targetHandle: String
}

"""2D position for visual layout"""
type Position {
  x: Float!
  y: Float!
}

"""Access control enum for flows"""
enum AccessType {
  "Flow is private to the owner"
  PRIVATE
  
  "Flow is publicly accessible"
  PUBLIC
}

"""Input type for creating a new flow"""
input FlowCreateInput {
  name: String!
  description: String
  icon: String
  icon_bg_color: String
  gradient: String
  data: JSON
  is_component: Boolean
  webhook: Boolean
  endpoint_name: String
  tags: [String!]
  locked: Boolean
  mcp_enabled: Boolean
  action_name: String
  action_description: String
  access_type: AccessType
  user_id: UUID
  folder_id: UUID
  fs_path: String
}

"""Input type for updating a flow"""
input FlowUpdateInput {
  name: String
  description: String
  data: JSON
  folder_id: UUID
  endpoint_name: String
  mcp_enabled: Boolean
  locked: Boolean
  action_name: String
  action_description: String
  access_type: AccessType
  fs_path: String
}
nodes.impact_analysis: No structural changes. Permission checks via UserRoleAssignment replace user_id filtering (C1).

nodes.name: Folder
nodes.description: Represents a folder/project for organizing flows. Folders support hierarchical nesting with parent-child relationships and can have authentication settings. Each folder belongs to a user and can contain multiple flows.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""Folder entity - Organizational unit for flows

Represents a folder/project that contains and organizes flows. Supports hierarchical
nesting, custom authentication settings, and ownership tracking. Folders can have
parent-child relationships for complex organizational structures.
"""

type Folder {
  "Unique identifier for the folder"
  id: UUID!
  
  "Name of the folder (must be unique per user)"
  name: String!
  
  "Optional description of the folder's purpose"
  description: String
  
  "Authentication settings for the folder/project"
  auth_settings: FolderAuthSettings
  
  "ID of the parent folder (null for root folders)"
  parent_id: UUID
  
  "Parent folder (for nested folder structures)"
  parent: Folder
  
  "Child folders nested under this folder"
  children: [Folder!]!
  
  "ID of the user who owns this folder"
  user_id: UUID
  
  "User who owns this folder"
  user: User!
  
  "Flows contained in this folder"
  flows: [Flow!]!
}

"""Authentication settings for a folder/project"""
type FolderAuthSettings {
  "Custom authentication configuration as JSON"
  settings: JSON
}

"""Input type for creating a new folder"""
input FolderCreateInput {
  "Name of the folder (must be unique per user)"
  name: String!
  
  "Optional description"
  description: String
  
  "Optional authentication settings"
  auth_settings: JSON
  
  "Optional parent folder ID for nesting"
  parent_id: UUID
  
  "Optional list of component IDs to include"
  components_list: [UUID!]
  
  "Optional list of flow IDs to include"
  flows_list: [UUID!]
}

"""Input type for updating a folder"""
input FolderUpdateInput {
  "New name for the folder"
  name: String
  
  "New description"
  description: String
  
  "New parent folder ID"
  parent_id: UUID
  
  "Updated list of component IDs"
  components: [UUID!]
  
  "Updated list of flow IDs"
  flows: [UUID!]
  
  "Updated authentication settings"
  auth_settings: JSON
}
nodes.impact_analysis: No structural changes. Requires immutability check for User's Default Project (DEFAULT_FOLDER_NAME). Owner assignment must set is_immutable=True (C2, M6).

nodes.name: MessageTable
nodes.description: Represents a message in a chat/conversation session. Messages track sender information, content with rich text support, file attachments, properties, and content blocks. Messages are associated with specific flows and sessions.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""Message entity - Chat/conversation message

Represents a message in a conversation or chat session. Supports rich content including
text, files, properties, content blocks, and error/edit tracking. Messages are associated
with flows and sessions for context.
"""

type Message {
  "Unique identifier for the message"
  id: UUID!
  
  "Timestamp when the message was sent"
  timestamp: DateTime!
  
  "Sender identifier (user, bot, system, etc.)"
  sender: String!
  
  "Display name of the sender"
  sender_name: String!
  
  "Session ID for grouping related messages"
  session_id: String!
  
  "Message text content"
  text: String!
  
  "List of file paths/URLs attached to the message"
  files: [String!]!
  
  "Indicates if this message represents an error"
  error: Boolean!
  
  "Indicates if this message is an edited version"
  edit: Boolean!
  
  "Additional properties for the message"
  properties: MessageProperties!
  
  "Category of the message (message, system, error, etc.)"
  category: String!
  
  "Rich content blocks for structured message content"
  content_blocks: [ContentBlock!]!
  
  "ID of the flow this message is associated with"
  flow_id: UUID
}

"""Message properties for metadata and context"""
type MessageProperties {
  "Source of the message"
  source: MessageSource
  
  "Icon for the message"
  icon: String
  
  "Background color"
  background_color: String
  
  "Additional metadata as JSON"
  metadata: JSON
}

"""Source information for a message"""
type MessageSource {
  "Source ID"
  id: String
  
  "Display name of the source"
  display_name: String
  
  "Source type"
  type: String
}

"""Content block for rich message content"""
type ContentBlock {
  "Type of content block"
  type: String!
  
  "Title of the block"
  title: String
  
  "Content of the block"
  content: JSON!
  
  "Additional properties"
  properties: JSON
}

"""Input type for creating a new message"""
input MessageCreateInput {
  "Sender identifier"
  sender: String!
  
  "Sender display name"
  sender_name: String!
  
  "Session ID"
  session_id: String!
  
  "Message text"
  text: String!
  
  "Optional file attachments"
  files: [String!]
  
  "Is this an error message?"
  error: Boolean
  
  "Is this an edited message?"
  edit: Boolean
  
  "Message properties"
  properties: JSON
  
  "Message category"
  category: String
  
  "Content blocks"
  content_blocks: [JSON!]
  
  "Associated flow ID"
  flow_id: UUID
}

"""Input type for updating a message"""
input MessageUpdateInput {
  text: String
  sender: String
  sender_name: String
  session_id: String
  files: [String!]
  edit: Boolean
  error: Boolean
  properties: JSON
}

nodes.name: ApiKey
nodes.description: Represents an API key for authentication and authorization. Tracks usage statistics, creation date, last usage, and active status. Each API key belongs to a specific user and can be deactivated without deletion.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""ApiKey entity - API authentication key

Represents an API key for authenticating API requests. Tracks usage statistics,
active status, and creation/usage timestamps. Keys can be masked for security
and belong to a specific user account.
"""

type ApiKey {
  "Unique identifier for the API key"
  id: UUID!
  
  "Optional name/label for the API key"
  name: String
  
  "The actual API key value (masked in read operations)"
  api_key: String!
  
  "Timestamp when the key was created"
  created_at: DateTime!
  
  "Timestamp when the key was last used"
  last_used_at: DateTime
  
  "Total number of times this key has been used"
  total_uses: Int!
  
  "Indicates if the API key is currently active"
  is_active: Boolean!
  
  "ID of the user who owns this API key"
  user_id: UUID!
  
  "User who owns this API key"
  user: User!
}

"""Input type for creating a new API key"""
input ApiKeyCreateInput {
  "Optional name for the API key"
  name: String
  
  "Custom API key value (auto-generated if not provided)"
  api_key: String
  
  "User ID (optional, defaults to current user)"
  user_id: UUID
}

"""Input type for updating an API key"""
input ApiKeyUpdateInput {
  "Update the name"
  name: String
  
  "Update active status"
  is_active: Boolean
}

nodes.description: Represents a build/execution of a vertex (node) in a flow. Tracks the execution data, artifacts produced, parameters used, validity status, and timestamps. VertexBuilds are associated with specific flows and maintain execution history.

  "ID of the flow this build belongs to"

  "Execution data"
  data: JSON
  
  "Generated artifacts"

  "Input parameters"
  params: String
  
  "Validity status"
  valid: Boolean!
  
  "Associated flow ID"
  flow_id: UUID!
}

nodes.name: TransactionTable
nodes.description: Represents a transaction/execution record for data flow between vertices. Tracks inputs, outputs, status, errors, and the source/target vertices involved. Transactions are associated with flows and provide execution audit trail.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""Transaction entity - Vertex-to-vertex execution record

Represents a transaction/data flow between vertices in a flow execution. Tracks input data,
output results, execution status, errors, and the vertices involved. Provides an audit trail
for flow executions and enables debugging of data transformations.
"""

type Transaction {
  "Unique identifier for this transaction"
  id: UUID!
  
  "Timestamp when the transaction occurred"
  timestamp: DateTime!
  
  "Source vertex ID"
  vertex_id: String!
  
  "Target vertex ID (if applicable)"
  target_id: String
  
  "Input data for the transaction (serialized with size limits)"
  inputs: JSON
  
  "Output data from the transaction (serialized with size limits)"
  outputs: JSON
  
  "Execution status (success, error, pending, etc.)"
  status: String!
  
  "Error message if the transaction failed"
  error: String
  
  "ID of the flow this transaction belongs to"
  flow_id: UUID!
}

"""Input type for creating a transaction record"""
input TransactionCreateInput {
  "Source vertex ID"
  vertex_id: String!
  
  "Optional target vertex ID"
  target_id: String
  
  "Input data"
  inputs: JSON
  
  "Output data"
  outputs: JSON
  
  "Execution status"
  status: String!
  
  "Optional error message"
  error: String
  
  "Associated flow ID"
  flow_id: UUID!
}

nodes.name: Role
nodes.description: Predefined roles in the RBAC system (Admin, Owner, Editor, Viewer). Roles define permission sets that can be assigned to users for specific scopes.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""Role entity - RBAC role definition

Represents a predefined role in the Role-Based Access Control system.
MVP includes 4 roles: Admin (global access), Owner (full CRUD), Editor (CRU), Viewer (Read-only).
Roles are immutable system entities that define permission sets.
"""

type Role {
  "Unique identifier for the role"
  id: UUID!

  "Role name (Admin, Owner, Editor, Viewer)"
  name: String!

  "Human-readable description of role capabilities"
  description: String

  "True if role applies globally (Admin only)"
  is_global: Boolean!

  "True if role is system-defined and immutable"
  is_system: Boolean!

  "Permissions granted to this role"
  permissions: [RolePermission!]!

  "User assignments for this role"
  assignments: [UserRoleAssignment!]!
}

input RoleCreate {
  name: String!
  description: String
  is_global: Boolean = false
}

input RoleRead {
  id: UUID!
  name: String!
  description: String
  is_global: Boolean!
  is_system: Boolean!
}

input RoleUpdate {
  description: String
}

schema_definition.graphql_schema:
type Role {
  id: UUID!
  name: String!
  description: String
  is_global: Boolean!
  created_at: DateTime!
  updated_at: DateTime!

  # Relationships
  permissions: [RolePermission!]!
  assignments: [UserRoleAssignment!]!
}

# Database Constraints:
# - UNIQUE(name)
# - CHECK(name IN ('Admin', 'Owner', 'Editor', 'Viewer'))
# - is_global = TRUE for 'Admin' role only
constraints: CHECK((name = 'Admin' AND is_global = TRUE) OR (name != 'Admin' AND is_global = FALSE))

nodes.impact_analysis: New RBAC schema node. Defines 4 predefined roles with permission sets. Supports Epic 1 Stories 1.1-1.3.

nodes.name: Permission
nodes.description: Base permissions in the RBAC system. Defines CRUD actions (Create, Read, Update, Delete) for Flow and Project scopes.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""Permission entity - RBAC permission definition

Represents a base permission action on a specific scope.
Permissions are atomic actions (CRUD) applied to entity types (Flow, Project).
Used in role-permission mappings to define role capabilities.
"""

enum PermissionAction {
  "Create new entities"
  CREATE

  "Read/view entities and execute flows"
  READ

  "Update/edit entities and import flows"
  UPDATE

  "Delete entities"
  DELETE
}

enum PermissionScope {
  "Flow-level permissions"
  FLOW

  "Project-level permissions (inherited by flows)"
  PROJECT
}

type Permission {
  "Unique identifier for the permission"
  id: UUID!

  "Permission action (CRUD)"
  action: PermissionAction!

  "Entity scope (Flow, Project)"
  scope: PermissionScope!

  "Human-readable description"
  description: String

  "Role mappings for this permission"
  role_permissions: [RolePermission!]!
}

input PermissionRead {
  id: UUID!
  action: PermissionAction!
  scope: PermissionScope!
  description: String
}

schema_definition.graphql_schema:
type Permission {
  id: UUID!
  action: PermissionAction!
  scope: PermissionScope!
  created_at: DateTime!
  updated_at: DateTime!

  # Relationships
  roles: [RolePermission!]!
}

enum PermissionAction {
  CREATE
  READ
  UPDATE
  DELETE
}

enum PermissionScope {
  FLOW
  PROJECT
}

# Database Constraints:
# - UNIQUE(action, scope)
# - action: 'create', 'read', 'update', 'delete'
# - scope: 'flow', 'project'

nodes.impact_analysis: New RBAC schema node. Defines 8 base permissions (4 actions x 2 scopes). Unique constraint on (action, scope) per M1 correction. Supports Epic 1 Story 1.2.

nodes.name: RolePermission
nodes.description: Junction table mapping roles to their permissions. Defines which permissions each role has (e.g., Viewer has READ only).
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""RolePermission entity - Role-to-permission mapping

Junction table that maps roles to their associated permissions.
Defines role capabilities: Admin has all, Owner has CRUD, Editor has CRU, Viewer has R.
Immutable mappings for system roles.
"""

type RolePermission {
  "Unique identifier"
  id: UUID!

  "Foreign key to Role"
  role_id: UUID!

  "Foreign key to Permission"
  permission_id: UUID!

  "Role entity"
  role: Role!

  "Permission entity"
  permission: Permission!
}

input RolePermissionRead {
  id: UUID!
  role_id: UUID!
  permission_id: UUID!
  role_name: String
  permission_action: String
  permission_scope: String
}

schema_definition.graphql_schema:
type RolePermission {
  id: UUID!
  role_id: UUID!
  permission_id: UUID!
  created_at: DateTime!

  # Relationships
  role: Role!
  permission: Permission!
}

# Database Constraints:
# - UNIQUE(role_id, permission_id)
# - FOREIGN KEY(role_id) REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
# - FOREIGN KEY(permission_id) REFERENCES permissions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
constraints: FOREIGN KEY(role_id) REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
FOREIGN KEY(permission_id) REFERENCES permissions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

nodes.impact_analysis: New RBAC schema node. Maps roles to permissions. Unique constraint on (role_id, permission_id) per M1 correction. Supports Epic 1 Story 1.3.

nodes.name: UserRoleAssignment
nodes.description: Assigns roles to users for specific scopes (global, project, flow). Supports permission inheritance from project to flow with override capability.
nodes.graphql_schema_physical:
"""UserRoleAssignment entity - User role assignment with scope

Assigns a role to a user for a specific scope (global, project, flow).
Supports inheritance: project roles inherited by flows unless overridden.
Admin role is global. Project roles can be inherited or overridden at flow level.
User's Default Project Owner assignment is immutable (C2, M6).
"""

enum AssignmentScope {
  "Global scope (Admin role only)"
  GLOBAL

  "Project-level assignment (inherited by flows)"
  PROJECT

  "Flow-level assignment (overrides project role)"
  FLOW
}

type UserRoleAssignment {
  "Unique identifier"
  id: UUID!

  "User being assigned the role"
  user_id: UUID!

  "Role being assigned"
  role_id: UUID!

  "Scope type (global, project, flow)"
  scope_type: AssignmentScope!

  "Scope ID (project_id or flow_id, null for global)"
  scope_id: UUID

  "True if assignment is immutable (User's Default Project Owner)"
  is_immutable: Boolean!

  "Assignment creation timestamp"
  created_at: DateTime!

  "User who created the assignment (self for auto-assignments)"
  created_by: UUID

  "User entity"
  user: User!

  "Role entity"
  role: Role!
}

input UserRoleAssignmentCreate {
  user_id: UUID!
  role_id: UUID!
  scope_type: AssignmentScope!
  scope_id: UUID
}

input UserRoleAssignmentRead {
  id: UUID!
  user_id: UUID!
  role_id: UUID!
  scope_type: AssignmentScope!
  scope_id: UUID
  is_immutable: Boolean!
  created_at: DateTime!
  created_by: UUID
  user_username: String
  role_name: String
  scope_entity_name: String
}

input UserRoleAssignmentUpdate {
  role_id: UUID
}

schema_definition.graphql_schema:
type UserRoleAssignment {
  id: UUID!
  user_id: UUID!
  role_id: UUID!
  scope: PermissionScope!
  scope_id: UUID!
  is_immutable: Boolean!
  created_at: DateTime!
  updated_at: DateTime!

  # Relationships
  user: User!
  role: Role!
}

# Database Constraints:
# - UNIQUE(user_id, role_id, scope, scope_id)
# - FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
# - FOREIGN KEY(role_id) REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
# - CHECK(scope IN ('flow', 'project'))
# - CHECK(is_immutable = TRUE only for default project Owner assignments)
constraints: FOREIGN KEY(user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
FOREIGN KEY(role_id) REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

nodes.name: Verify Core RBAC Entities Definition
nodes.story: Story 1.1: Define & Persist Core Permissions and Scopes

gherkin.given: the persistence layer is available
gherkin.when: the system is initialized
then: the four base permissions (Create, Read, Update, Delete) should be defined in the metadata store
the two entity scopes (Flow, Project) should be defined in the metadata store
the data model should establish the relationship between permissions and scopes

nodes.name: Verify Default Roles and Permission Mappings
nodes.story: Story 1.2: Define & Persist Default Roles and Mappings

gherkin.scenario: Mapping Default Roles and Extended Permissions
gherkin.given: the four base permissions are defined
gherkin.when: the default roles are persisted
then: the Owner role should have full CRUD access to its scope entity
the Admin role should have full CRUD access across all scopes/entities
the Editor role should have Create, Read, Update access (but not Delete)
the Viewer role should have only Read/View access
the Read/View permission should enable Flow execution, saving, exporting, and downloading
the Update/Edit permission should enable Flow/Project import

nodes.name: Verify Role Assignment Logic
nodes.story: Story 1.3: Implement Core Role Assignment Logic

gherkin.scenario: Admin Assigns or Modifies a Role Assignment
gherkin.given: the internal assignment API (assignRole / removeRole) is exposed
gherkin.when: an Admin calls the API to create a new role assignment (User, Role, Scope)
then: the assignment should be successfully persisted
gherkin.and_when: an Admin calls the API to modify or delete an existing assignment
and_then: the Admin should be authorized to perform the action
the updated assignment should be successfully persisted or removed
gherkin.but: the Admin should be prevented from modifying the Starter Project Owner assignment (as per 1.4)

nodes.name: Verify Starter Project Owner Immutability
nodes.story: Story 1.4: Default Project Owner Immutability Check

gherkin.scenario: Preventing changes to the Starter Project Owner Role
gherkin.given: a user has the Owner role assigned to their default/Starter Project (which is pre-existing)
gherkin.when: an Admin attempts to modify, delete, or transfer this specific Owner role assignment
then: the attempt should be blocked at the application logic layer
the user should maintain the Owner role on their Starter Project

nodes.name: Verify Project Creation and Owner Assignment
nodes.story: Story 1.5: Global Project Creation & New Entity Owner Mutability

gherkin.scenario: Project Creation and New Entity Owner Assignment
gherkin.given: any authenticated user is logged in
gherkin.when: the user attempts to create a new Project
then: the user should have access to the Create Project function
gherkin.and_when: a user successfully creates a new Project or Flow
and_then: the creating user should be automatically assigned the Owner role for that new entity
an Admin should be able to modify this new entity's Owner role assignment

nodes.name: Verify Project Role Inheritance Logic
nodes.story: Story 1.6: Define Project to Flow Role Extension Rule

gherkin.given: a user has a specific (or default) role assigned to a Project
gherkin.when: the user attempts to access a Flow contained within that Project
then: the user should automatically inherit the permissions of the assigned Project role for that Flow
gherkin.but: if an explicit, different role is assigned to the user for that specific Flow scope, the Flow-specific role should override the inherited role (per 2.1 logic)

nodes.name: Verify CanAccess Authorization Logic
nodes.epic: Epic 2: RBAC Enforcement Engine & Runtime Checks
nodes.story: Story 2.1: Core CanAccess Authorization Service

gherkin.given: the CanAccess method is called with a user, permission, and scope
gherkin.when: the user_id has the Admin role
then: the method should immediately return true
gherkin.and_when: the user is non-Admin accessing a Flow
and_then: the service should first check for a direct Flow-specific role
if no Flow-specific role exists, the service should check the inherited role from the containing Project
gherkin.and_when_2: the user is non-Admin accessing a Project
and_then_2: the service should check the Project-specific role

nodes.name: Verify Read Permission and List Filtering
nodes.epic: Epic 2: RBAC Enforcement Engine & Runtime Checks
nodes.story: Story 2.2: Enforce Read/View Permission & List Visibility

gherkin.scenario: UI Filtering and Read Access Enforcement
gherkin.given: a user loads the Project or Flow list view
gherkin.when: the user lacks the Read/View permission for an entity
then: that entity should not be displayed in the list view
gherkin.and_when: a user attempts to view the editor, execute, save/export, or download a Flow/Project
and_then: the AuthService should confirm Read/View permission
the action should be blocked if permission is denied

nodes.name: Verify Create Permission Enforcement
nodes.epic: Epic 2: RBAC Enforcement Engine & Runtime Checks
nodes.story: Story 2.3: Enforce Create Permission on Projects & Flows

gherkin.given: a non-Admin user is logged in
gherkin.when: the user views the Project interface
then: the UI elements (e.g., buttons, options) for creating a new Flow must be hidden or disabled if the user lacks the Create permission on that Project scope
if the user attempts to bypass the UI (e.g., API call), the AuthService should block the creation

nodes.name: Verify Update Permission Enforcement
nodes.epic: Epic 2: RBAC Enforcement Engine & Runtime Checks
nodes.story: Story 2.4: Enforce Update/Edit Permission for Projects & Flows

gherkin.given: a user loads the editor for a Project or Flow
gherkin.when: the user lacks the Update/Edit permission
then: the editor should load in a read-only state
the user should be prevented from making any changes/edits
the check must also occur before allowing import functionality

nodes.name: Verify Delete Permission Enforcement
nodes.epic: Epic 2: RBAC Enforcement Engine & Runtime Checks
nodes.story: Story 2.5: Enforce Delete Permission for Projects & Flows

gherkin.given: a user views the interface for a Project or Flow
gherkin.when: the user does not have the Delete permission
then: the UI elements (e.g., buttons, options) for deleting the entity must be hidden or disabled
if the user attempts to bypass the UI, the AuthService should block the action
the action should only be permitted if the user is an Admin or has the Owner role for the scope entity

nodes.name: Verify RBAC Management Section Access
nodes.story: Story 3.1: RBAC Management Section in the Admin Page

gherkin.given: a Admin Page exists which contains the User Management section today, a new RBAC Management section gets added to the Admin Page, and Admin Page has two tabs now with the User Management Section (default one to open when user accesses the Admin Page) and the RBAC Management section and a deep link exists for the RBAC management section within the Admin Page
gherkin.when: an Admin user accesses the Admin Page
then: she should be able to access the RBAC Management section
gherkin.when_2: a non-Admin user accesses the Admin Page
then_2: she should NOT be able to access the RBAC Management section
gherkin.when_3: a Admin user tries to access the deeplink for the RBAC management section
then_3: she should be able to access the RBAC Management section
gherkin.when_4: a non-Admin user tries to access the deeplink for the RBAC management section
then_4: the system should display an Access Denied message

nodes.name: Verify Assignment Creation Workflow
nodes.story: Story 3.2: Assignment Creation Workflow (New Roles)

gherkin.scenario: Assigning a New Role to a User
gherkin.given: an Admin is in the RBAC management section
gherkin.when: the Admin initiates the new assignment workflow
then: the workflow should guide the Admin through sequential steps: Select User → Select Scope → Select Role → Confirm
the only assignable role options should be the four default roles or the global Admin role
and_then: the Core Role Assignment Logic (Epic 1.3) should be successfully called

nodes.name: Verify Assignment List and Filtering
nodes.story: Story 3.3: Assignment List View and Filtering

gherkin.given: an Admin is in the RBAC management section
gherkin.when: the master assignment list view is displayed
then: the list should show all active User: Scope: Role assignments
the list should be filterable by User, Role, and Scope Entity
a clear mechanism should be available to directly delete any assignment from the list view

nodes.name: Verify Assignment Edit and Delete
nodes.story: Story 3.4: Assignment Editing and Removal

gherkin.given: an Admin selects an assignment from the master list to edit
gherkin.when: the Admin changes the Role for that specific scope
then: the system should call the Core Role Assignment Logic (Epic 1.3) to update the assignment

nodes.name: Verify Flow Role Inheritance Display
nodes.story: Story 3.5: Flow Role Inheritance Display Rule

gherkin.given: a user has an inherited role from a Project
gherkin.when: the Admin views the assignment list
then: the list should not display a specific assignment entry for the inherited Flow role
gherkin.and_when: the Admin views the assignment interface
and_then: a clear message should be displayed: 'Project-level assignments are inherited by contained Flows and can be overridden by explicit Flow-specific roles.'

nodes.name: Verify CanAccess Check Latency
nodes.story: Story 5.1: Role Assignment and Enforcement Latency

gherkin.given: the authorization service (AuthService) is running at 50% average load
gherkin.when: the AuthService.CanAccess method is called for any user/permission/scope combination
then: the check must return a response in less than 50 milliseconds (p95)

nodes.name: Verify Assignment Creation Latency
nodes.story: Story 5.1: Role Assignment and Enforcement Latency

gherkin.given: an Admin executes an assignment update/create via the API
gherkin.when: the Core Role Assignment Logic (Epic 1.3) is executed
then: the API response time should be less than 200 milliseconds (p95)

nodes.name: Verify System Availability
nodes.story: Story 5.2: System Uptime and Availability

gherkin.given: all core services (Auth, RBAC Data Store, AuthService) are monitored
gherkin.when: measuring system availability over a calendar month
then: the overall platform uptime must meet 99.9% availability (excluding scheduled maintenance)

nodes.name: Verify Editor Load Time with RBAC
nodes.story: Story 5.3: Readiness Time (Initial Load)

gherkin.scenario: Editor Load Time with RBAC Check
gherkin.given: a user loads the Project/Flow editor page
gherkin.when: the page requires the initial bulk permission check (e.g., hiding create/delete buttons)
then: the entire page load, including the RBAC checks, must be completed in less than 2.5 seconds (p95)
